styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, colonial churches and the lively Zona 1 old town.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Markets, comedores and street snacks from dawn to late.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Maya collections, plazas and the city's layered past.

stays.why: Modern, safest-feeling base. Hotels, restaurants and malls within walking distance; easy taxi and ride-app pickups.
Next to Zona 10 and the Torre del Reformador area. Quieter streets, still close to dining and nightlife.
Historic center: Plaza Mayor, the cathedral and the National Palace. Cheapest, but use care on foot, especially after dark.
Trendy, walkable pocket of cafés, bars and galleries. Good for nightlife and food; book ahead on weekends.

food: Try Guatemalan staples: pepián (thick spiced stew), kak'ik (turkey soup), tamales and chuchitos.
Mercado Central in Zona 1: cheap comedores and fresh produce. Go with a local or in a group; keep valuables out of sight.
Breakfast: eggs, black beans, plantain and thick tortillas. Cafés in Zona 4 and Zona 10 do good coffee.
Street snacks: tostadas, shucos (hot dogs with toppings) and rellenitos (plantain with bean paste). Eat where locals queue.
Prices vary. Budget roughly Q30–80 for a simple meal and Q150+ at mid-range restaurants. Check the bill for service charges.
more_time: Swap a city day for Antigua Guatemala: colonial streets and volcano views, roughly an hour by road. Check bus and shuttle times on the day.
Add Lake Atitlán or Chichicastenango market as an overnight, not a day trip. Roads are slow; book a shuttle.
Maya history fans: the Museo Nacional de Arqueología y Etnología in Zona 13 pairs well with a half-day at the relief map (Mapa en Relieve) in Zona 2.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the museums, Zona 1 old town and the food scene, with a day spare for Antigua.

month_notes: Jan: dry and cool. Highs near 23°C, lows near 12°C. Pack a jacket for evenings.
Feb: the driest month, about 4 rain days. Great for walking the old town.
Mar: warm and mostly dry. Highs near 27°C; sunscreen for midday.
Apr: hottest month, highs near 28°C. Rain picks up late in the month.
May: rainy season starts. About 19 rain days; plan indoor sights for afternoons.
Jun: wet, about 23 rain days. Mornings are usually the better bet.
Jul: still wet but a little cooler. Carry a rain jacket.
Aug: wet, about 21 rain days. Expect afternoon downpours.
Sep: the wettest month, about 24 rain days. Keep plans flexible.
Oct: still rainy, about 21 rain days. Cooler evenings near 15°C.
Nov: rain eases to about 12 days. Pleasant highs near 22°C.
Dec: dry and cool again, about 6 rain days. Good for city sightseeing.

climate_guide.summary: Mild year-round at about 1,500 m. Two seasons: dry and cooler from November to April, wet from May to October.

items.title: Best time: November to April
items.text: Highs around 22–28°C and few rain days. Ideal for walking Zona 1 and day trips.

items.title: Wet season: May to October
items.text: Rain on 18–24 days a month, usually afternoon showers. Do outdoor sights in the morning.

items.title: Mild, not hot
items.text: Highs stay between 22 and 28°C all year. Nights are cool, around 12–16°C.

items.title: Cool evenings
items.text: Lows near 12–13°C in December to February. Bring a light jacket.

items.title: Pack for rain in the wet months
items.text: A compact umbrella and a dry bag for your phone help in June to September.

items.title: Sun at altitude
items.text: The city sits high, so the sun is strong even on mild days. Use sunscreen and a hat.

transit.best: Uber or a yellow metered taxi for most trips; Transmetro for cheap rides on main routes.

modes.text: No metro. Transmetro is a bus rapid transit system, not rail.

Transmetro BRT has 7 lines. Pay with the Citizen's Card (Q20 with 5 trips) or a contactless card; cash is not accepted. Transurbano buses need a prepaid card and are slower but cover more routes. Avoid red city buses.
Yellow metered taxis (call 1766) or white taxis where you negotiate the price first. Uber works and is handy for airport and late-night rides.
Traffic is chaotic. Cars are available but not recommended for city driving.
Use caution. Walk accompanied where you can, and avoid quiet streets after dark.
